page: Vultr vhf-8c-32gb is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the High Frequency Compute family. It features 8 shared Intel vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled with a 512 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present on this server type.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most standard compute metrics, including Geekbench single-core and multi-core evaluations, and Passmark CPU tests. Single-threaded gzip compression and Passmark memory scores reach top-tier levels. However, significant performance bottlenecks exist in memory bandwidth for large, uncached blocks, which registers in the bottom 25% for both read and write operations. Additionally, while small-model LLM inference is average, medium-model LLM inference is poor, falling into the bottom 10%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the shared CPU allocation and balanced resource density make this server a viable option for workloads that do not require dedicated CPU cores. The combination of 32.0 GB of RAM and local NVMe storage makes it suitable for general-purpose applications, software compilation, static web serving, and database operations that fit within the memory and storage limits, though it is not recommended for memory-intensive uncached operations or medium-to-large language model inference.
